title: UI performance profiling after the keyboard fix: measure typing, tab switch, scroll and state-update cost on a representative state, then fix the largest proven causes
outcome: A recorded baseline of UI interaction cost on master, with cd79424e's keyboard fix, against a representative state. The largest measured causes are identified with evidence, and the worthwhile fixes are either landed or filed with their cost and impact.
acceptance: A baseline is recorded before any change. It uses the existing app-latency harness, or an equivalent reproducible setup, with a representative state: many sessions, long transcripts, active test runs and mailbox traffic. It reports numbers for typing latency, tab or session switch, transcript scroll, and incoming state-update and SSE handling. Each number comes with its method and environment, and no number is extrapolated.

The top causes are identified with profiler evidence: main-thread time split into script, layout and render, the component or function responsible, and correlation with backend payload size where that is relevant, for example the existing large-snapshot item w-919a18aecf19. Each cause carries an estimated cost to fix and an expected impact.

Every proven fix is either landed through the normal pair and FULL with a before/after measurement on the same setup, or filed as its own item with its numbers. No speculative optimisation lands without a measured improvement, and existing UI behaviour stays the same.

completion.summary: Delivered the pre-change baseline, private-trace root-cause analysis and 14-cell rich-state dev/production baseline with raw profiles, source mapping and explicit limits. The original 350.814 ms quadratic hidden-tail scan was fixed through the normal pair and exact FULL on w7245. Remaining measured run-history cost is filed as w-0fab7204fcff, secondary publication research as w-25ac4c50dc78, and payload evidence added to existing w919. No speculative product optimization was made.
